facts.fact: Fixed b298 request allows one dataset row, 128 dataset bytes, two training steps; optimizer epochs is two. This is not the 8192-row evaluation-provider fixture.
The actual source observation and baseline matrix input width are two.
Production decoder bounds base64 input to 1024 characters and requires rows == 1 and width in 1..=64, matching the loaded input width.

The test explicitly exercises 20 Training readbacks, six Selection readbacks and three C commands. Every Training readback brackets native/Generator CURRENT with two live captures, each reading Material twice; existing test requires at least 80 and fewer than 128 reads per relevant original Material peer.

A successful capture directly invokes verify_original_evidence twice and performs two Material decodes, each invoking require_original_material_signatures twice. These six directly visible scope.validate_snapshot calls repeat pure request/scope encoding checks, but the surrounding complete signatures, original-owner RPCs and fresh-time checks cannot be removed wholesale.

The request checkpoint encoding contains 13 IDs, nine digests (including the selected bundle digest), envelope fields and fixed budget fields. It does not traverse training samples or model tensor bytes.

conclusion.deadlock: Not established by this sample. The observed thread is executing a hash while other original-owner/channel threads wait; this is not a system-wide deadlock proof or disproof.
conclusion.performance: No measurement attributes a material fraction of the 60-second budget to request hashing. The observed bounded repeated pure checks are not evidence that caching them would fix the timeout.
conclusion.preserved_contract: No owner read or signature verification removed; no cached receipt, altered deadline, increased stack, changed sample policy or weakened assertion proposed.
